draft.title: Torque
card: Torque is the turning effect of a force about a pivot. It is measured in newton metres (N m).
τ = r F sin θ. Here r is the distance from the pivot to where the force acts, F is the force, and θ is the angle between the force and the line from the pivot.
For the same force, a larger r gives a larger torque. This is why a longer spanner turns a tight nut more easily.
A force pushing at right angles (θ = 90°) to the line from the pivot gives the most torque. A force along that line (θ = 0°) gives zero torque.
draft.remember: Torque depends on the force, the distance from the pivot, and the angle.

a.q: Why does a longer spanner make a tight nut easier to turn?
opts: The same force acts at a greater distance, so torque is more
The longer spanner makes the force on the nut larger
The longer spanner gives the nut more mass to turn
The angle of the force is larger with a longer spanner
a.why: Torque is r F sin θ, so a larger r gives a larger torque for the same force. The force itself is not made bigger by the spanner. Only the distance from the pivot changes.
a.clue: Which part of τ = r F sin θ changes with spanner length?

b.q: Priya pushes on a door with a force of 20 N. The door is 0.90 m wide and she pushes at the handle edge, at 90° to the door. What is the torque about the hinges?
opts: 18 N m
22 N m
0 N m
1.8 N m
b.why: τ = r F sin θ = 0.90 × 20 × sin 90° = 18 N m. The torque is not zero, because the push is at right angles to the line from the hinges, which gives the largest sin θ value of 1.
b.clue: sin 90° equals 1, so multiply distance by force.

a.best: The same force acts at a greater distance, so torque is more

problems.detail: The clue 'sin 90° equals 1, so multiply distance by force' hands students the whole method. They can get 18 N m without having to apply τ = r F sin θ themselves, which makes the question trivial for Year 12.
